info.title: GameLock
info.author: Kazbonfim
info.details:
Per-title parental control for Atmosphere. The Switch's built-in parental control works by age rating: you lock a whole tier or nothing. GameLock lets you pick exactly which installed games need a PIN, and leaves the rest untouched.

Mark a game and it stops launching from HOME. The PIN is asked once, when GameLock opens. From there the two buttons do different jobs: B opens the selected game right away, blocked or not, and leaves nothing marked behind. Y releases a game so it opens from HOME too, for when the kid plays alone, and it stays released until you lock it back. A master switch turns all protection off and keeps your selections.

How it works: marking a game writes empty exefs stubs under sdmc:/atmosphere/contents. Atmosphere's loader returns ResultPathNotFound() for stubbed NSOs, so the game process is never created. No sysmodule, no IPC, no MITM, no NAND or save edits. Only stubs GameLock created are deleted, so your LayeredFS mods stay intact.

The PIN is never stored: just a salt and a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash. It is asked when GameLock opens, and after that only to change or delete it.

The interface comes in English and Brazilian Portuguese, switchable in Settings.

Two things to know: opening a blocked game with B leaves that title without its stub until the next time you open GameLock, which puts it back; and there is no session expiry, so GameLock left open is GameLock unlocked. Anyone who can pull the SD card bypasses this too: it stops casual access, not a technical user.

changelog:
v1.0.1

- B opens the selected game even when it is blocked. Before, you had to release it with Y first, which taught the bad habit: release, play, close, forget the game released for the kid. Past the PIN gate you are the owner, so B just opens it
- Nothing is recorded when B opens a blocked game. The stub comes off for that launch only, and the next time GameLock opens it reconciles and the game stops launching from HOME again, with nothing to remember to undo
- Known cost: between that launch and the next time you open GameLock, the title has no stub and does open from HOME. The stub cannot be put back after the launch request, since the system takes the foreground and GameLock's process is gone before it could write
- Y keeps its own job: release a game so it opens from HOME, for when the kid plays alone
- Interface in English and Brazilian Portuguese, switchable in Settings. The language line is labelled in both, so anyone who lands in the wrong one can still find it
- One PIN gate. The PIN is asked when GameLock opens, and after that only to change or delete it. Unprotecting a game with A, releasing one with Y and the master switch no longer ask again: past the gate the same secret proves nothing, and each of those was already reachable for free game by game
- Locking the released games back never asks for the PIN: it tightens protection, and a password to lock a door is friction for nothing
- No session expiry: GameLock left open is GameLock unlocked. Said plainly instead of simulated with prompts that do not protect
- config.json gains an optional lang key. Files written by earlier versions stay valid

v0.9.0

- Press B to launch the selected game straight from GameLock, instead of leaving and hunting for its icon on HOME. Works in applet and application mode (FW 5.0.0+)
- A blocked game refuses to launch and says to unlock it with Y first
- Stubs are reconciled before the launch request, since the loader reads the SD card at launch time
- Loading screen while the game list is read and the SD card is reconciled

v0.8.0

First public release.

- Game list with icon, name, title ID and lock state
- PIN: set, change, remove, asked on launch (3 attempts)
- PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 16-byte salt and constant-time comparison
- Built-in numeric keypad, so the PIN works in both applet and application mode
- Blocking via exefs stubs, surviving reboot and sleep/resume
- Temporary unlock with Y, without clearing the marking
- Master switch to disable all protection without unmarking
- Ownership tracking: only stubs created by GameLock are ever deleted
- Atomic config.json writes with reconciliation on launch
